# `precondition_failed`

A precondition the caller sent no longer holds.

| Status | Title | `type` |
|---|---|---|
| `412` | Precondition failed | `https://substrat.net/errors/precondition-failed` |

## What it means

The caller made the write conditional, with `If-Match` and the version it read, and the record has changed since. `entity` names the record. The current version is deliberately not in the body: a client that retried with it blindly would overwrite the change that caused the refusal.

## When it is returned

- A write sent with `If-Match` whose version is no longer the record's current one.
- A promote whose acknowledged review is no longer the one it would apply (`reason: promote_review_stale`).

## What it carries

- `entity`: The record the refusal is about, as an entity reference (`{ entityType, entityId }`).
- `reason`: A slug the refusing module owns, narrowing the code. The platform's own are snake_case, but the wire does not enforce a grammar, so compare it as an opaque string. Branch on it; never show it.

Relayed from a scope store, it may also carry `storeCode` and `storeBody`. See [the body](/errors/#the-body) for the members any problem may carry.

## What to do

Re-read the record, show or merge what changed, and send the write again with the version you just read. Never retry with a new version you did not read.

## In `/openapi.json`

Documented only on the operations that accept a precondition (`If-Match`), since no other operation can answer it.
